summary: In an upscale restaurant, a steak is being cut and eaten while a negotiation unfolds between Agent Smith and Cypher (whom Smith addresses as Mr. Reagan). Cypher savors the steak even though he openly admits it does not exist and is only the Matrix feeding his brain the sensation of taste, declaring that 'Ignorance is bliss.' He makes his terms explicit: he wants no memory of his real life, and he wants to be reinserted into the Matrix as someone rich and important, 'like an actor.' Smith promises to grant whatever he wants. In return, Cypher offers to have his body returned to a power plant and reinserted, and in exchange he will deliver what Smith wants. Smith names it as the access codes to the Zion mainframe. Cypher says he does not know the codes himself but can hand over the man who does, and Smith identifies that man as Morpheus.

what_changes.before: A member of the Nebuchadnezzar crew who has been voicing regret about leaving the Matrix, now secretly meeting with an Agent.
what_changes.after: He has openly committed to betraying Zion by striking a deal with Agent Smith to deliver Morpheus in exchange for being reinserted into the Matrix as a wealthy, important, forgetful man.
what_changes.evidence: You get my body back in a power plant, reinsert me into the Matrix and I'll get you what you want.

what_changes.before: He opens by pressing Cypher for a decision, 'Do we have a deal, Mr. Reagan?', without yet stating what he is after.
what_changes.after: He has named his true objective and the specific target, stating 'Access codes to the Zion mainframe' and identifying the man Cypher can deliver as 'Morpheus.'
what_changes.evidence: AGENT SMITH Access codes to the Zion mainframe. CYPHER I told you I don't know them. But I can give you the man who does. AGENT SMITH Morpheus.

event_hint.one_line: Cypher and Agent Smith finalize a betrayal deal: Cypher will hand over Morpheus in exchange for being reinserted into the Matrix as a rich, forgetful, important man.

minds.wants: To lock in an irreversible escape — to trade Morpheus for a rich, important, forgetful life inside the Matrix, and to make the terms so explicit that Smith cannot later renege on the forgetting.
minds.feels: A man who has fully reconciled himself to betrayal and is no longer conflicted about it; his regret (sc-073, the 'blue pill' toast, 'I've been thinking the same thing ever since I got here') has hardened into a transaction. Underneath the gourmand's relish is someone who cannot bear the real — the grey goop, the cold ship, the burden of being 'no one' — and is buying oblivion as the only comfort left.
minds.shows: Sensuous, almost playful indulgence — sawing the steak, shoving it in, eyes rolling up, smacking it, 'Mmm so, so goddamn good' — performing the part of a man who has it good, and treating the treason like a casual business lunch. He keeps it light, even charming.
minds.basis: He savors a steak he openly says 'doesn't exist' and names his philosophy ('Ignorance is bliss') before stating terms. His demands are specific and repeated for emphasis: 'I don't want to remember nothing. Nothing! You understand? And I want to be rich. Someone important. Like an actor.' He then lays out the exchange — body to power plant, reinsertion, and 'I'll get you what you want' — and admits he doesn't know the codes but 'can give you the man who does.' In sc-073 he already confessed to Neo that he's been regretting leaving the Matrix since he arrived and called the prophecy a 'mindjob,' seeding this turn.

believes_about.belief: That Smith is a reliable business partner who will honor the deal and actually reinsert him as someone rich who remembers nothing.
believes_about.wrong_because: Smith is an Agent — a program whose interest is Zion's destruction, not Cypher's comfort; the deal is a means to Morpheus, and there is no reason to trust that Smith will grant the forgetting or the comfortable life once Morpheus is delivered. The scene's dramatic irony is that Cypher is negotiating his fate with the one party structurally incapable of keeping such a promise.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus is a deluded fanatic who 'got them all amped up believing in bullshit' and whose faith (in the One, in the prophecy) is the thing that gets people killed — so handing him over is justified, even a correction of a lie.
believes_about.wrong_because: This is Cypher's rationalization built in sc-073 ('Morpeus. He got them all amped up believing in bullshit. I watched each of them take on an Agent'), reframing Morpheus's conviction as dangerous madness to excuse the betrayal; the coming events treat Morpheus's belief as the very thing that will be tested and vindicated, not the delusion Cypher dismisses.

minds.wants: To close the deal and obtain the access codes to the Zion mainframe by acquiring the one man who has them — Morpheus — using Cypher as the delivery mechanism.
minds.feels: Cold, patient, and in control; he has already mapped the entire transaction and is merely confirming the last link. There is no relish, no performance — only the quiet certainty of a predator who has cornered his prey and is letting it name its own price, because the price costs him nothing he isn't willing to fake.
minds.shows: Terse, formal, and almost bored. He lets Cypher perform the steak ritual and watches him ('Agent Smith watches him chew the steak loudly'), saying little, pressing only for commitment ('Do we have a deal, Mr. Reagan?' / 'Then we have a deal?'), and naming the objective and the target with flat precision ('Access codes to the Zion mainframe.' / 'Morpheus.').
minds.basis: He opens by pressing for the decision rather than re-arguing terms, showing the substance is already settled. His restraint — watching Cypher chew, offering only 'Whatever you want, Mr. Reagan' — reads as a man who need not perform because he holds the leverage. He names exactly what he wants and, when Cypher says he can deliver the man who knows the codes, supplies the name 'Morpheus' himself, showing he already knew the target and the value of what Cypher offers.

believes_about.belief: That Cypher is a dependable instrument — a man whose self-disgust and appetite make him predictably willing to sell out his crew, and whose delivery of Morpheus can be trusted to go through.
believes_about.wrong_because: A man who betrays his captain for comfort is, by definition, untrustworthy; the same selfishness that makes Cypher useful makes him unreliable. Smith is betting on a traitor's consistency, which is a contradiction — though for Smith's purposes Cypher need only be consistent in his cowardice, which he is.

connects_back: sc-073: Cypher's drink with Neo, where he admits he's regretted taking the red pill 'ever since I got here,' calls the prophecy a 'mindjob,' and blames Morpheus for getting five previous 'Ones' killed — the psychological groundwork for the betrayal finalized here.
ev-018: The cut from the main-deck confession straight into this restaurant negotiation; the scene realizes the betrayal that scene set up.
Cypher's established resentment of the real world (the ship's cold, the grey food) that makes 'ignorance is bliss' and the demand for a rich, forgetful life legible rather than arbitrary.
sets_up: ev-023: Cypher's murder of Dozer and shooting of Tank on the ship — the direct consequence of his having committed to delivering Morpheus and needing to neutralize the crew to do it.
The Agents' capture and interrogation of Morpheus, enabled by Cypher handing over the man who knows the Zion mainframe access codes.
The crew's fracturing and the deadly stakes of the coming mission, since the betrayal removes any safe return and forces the confrontation that leads to Morpheus's capture and Neo's choice.
dramatic_function: It converts Cypher's private regret — seeded in the cockpit and the main deck — into an irreversible plot turn by staging the actual treason, giving the film its human antagonist within the crew and creating the mechanism (Morpheus's betrayal) that will drive the capture, the crew's near-destruction, and Neo's emergence. It also dramatizes the film's central question — the value of the real versus a comfortable lie — by letting the traitor answer it for the comfortable lie, so the audience sees the cost of that choice made flesh.
